title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — evangelical-justice reply; sin's ratio unlike gifted righteousness
pass_a_gloss: Placeus answers the 'reckoned as if just' comeback: we really are just—evangelical faith-righteousness given by God, not legal works-righteousness from us. Sin does not work that way: it is not promised, given by God, or received by someone not yet existing.
pass_b_english: But someone will say: we are reckoned before God as if we were just. Yes—we truly are just, not by a legal righteousness but by an evangelical one; not by a righteousness of works but of faith; not by a righteousness that proceeds from us or is acquired by us, but given by God and received through faith. The case of sin is different: it is not promised, not given by God, not received by one who does not yet exist.
source_text: At, inquiet aliquis, censemur apud Deum ac si iusti essemus. Nempe reuera iusti sumus, non iustitia legali sed evangelica, non iustitia operum sed fidei, non iustitia a nobis profecta aut acquisita, sed data a Deo & per fidem accepta. Dispar est ratio peccati: non promittitur, non datur a Deo, non accipitur a nondum existente.
